items.prompt: In processMockPaymentWebhook, which call is the first database write on the success path?
items.answer: tx.webhookEvent.create, after the identity check, both scoped reads and the transition guard
distractors: tx.webhookEvent.upsert, issued before the payment lookup so that a retry can find its claim
tx.payment.update; the webhook event row is created later, once the invoice is marked paid
writeAuditLog(tx, ...), so the attempt is recorded before any business row is changed
items.explanation: Everything before tx.webhookEvent.create (payments.service.ts:73) is a read or a refusal: permission, parse, event identity, scoped payment, scoped invoice, transition guard. The upsert-first shape was the pre-repair route; the payment update and the audit write both come after the event create.

items.prompt: An accepted event evt-1234 is re-sent by the same tenant with a different paymentId that also exists in that tenant. What does the service do?
items.answer: It throws 409 webhook.identity_conflict before the new payment is looked up
distractors: It replays it as a duplicate, as the provider event id alone fixes the identity
It processes the new payment and points the stored event row at the new id
It answers 404 payment.not_found, since the event already names another payment
items.explanation: An existing event is compared on organization AND payload hash (payments.service.ts:44). A changed paymentId changes the hash, so the same provider id now has a second meaning and is refused with 409 before any target read.

items.prompt: A replay of an accepted event arrives with providerEventId " evt-1234 " (padded with spaces) and every other field unchanged. What happens?
items.answer: It is acknowledged as a duplicate: Zod trims the id before the body is hashed
distractors: 409 identity_conflict, because the padded raw body hashes to a different value
400 webhook.invalid, since the strict schema refuses strings with outer spaces
A brand-new event is created; the padded id is a different unique key
items.explanation: webhookSchema trims providerEventId (payments.service.ts:10) and the service hashes the PARSED body, so the padded id normalizes to the stored one and the replay short-circuits. Only providerEventId is trimmed; a padded paymentId would be a 404 (finding F7).

items.prompt: A payment.failed event with a new provider id arrives for a payment that is already succeeded. Which writes happen?
items.answer: Only the new event row (marked processedAt) plus an audit row tagged payment.failed.ignored, with no payment, invoice or outbox write
distractors: The new event row, then the payment set to failed, the invoice reopened and a payment.failed outbox row queued for delivery
None at all: it is refused with 409 invoice.transition_invalid before the new event row is ever created
Nothing is written, and the service returns duplicate: true for it, exactly as it does for a replayed event
items.explanation: The new event id creates its webhookEvent row (line 73). alreadySucceeded && !succeeded then skips the payment and invoice updates (line 85), still sets processedAt and writes the audit row with action payment.failed.ignored (line 105), and the guard at line 110 suppresses the failure outbox. A late notification cannot undo a financial success.

items.prompt: A payment that is already succeeded receives a payment.succeeded event with a NEW provider event id. What is written?
items.answer: No payment or invoice update, yet an audit row and a second payment.succeeded outbox row
distractors: Nothing beyond the event row: the outbox guard suppresses events for settled payments
409 webhook.identity_conflict, as the payment already carries an earlier providerRef value
Only the invoice: paidAt is overwritten with the new time and nothing else changes
items.explanation: The updates are skipped because alreadySucceeded is true (line 85), but the line-110 guard only suppresses alreadySucceeded && !succeeded, so a second success writes audit AND another outbox row. That is finding F2; no test covers it.

items.prompt: A request reaches the API with neither x-org-slug nor x-user-email set. Who is it treated as?
items.answer: The seeded Acme owner, since both headers fall back to built-in defaults
distractors: Nobody: attachTenantContext answers 403 membership.denied for blank headers
An anonymous caller, rejected with 401 before the membership lookup runs
A viewer of the default tenant, holding only the billing:read permission
items.explanation: auth.ts:15-16 defaults the slug to "acme" and the email to config.defaultUserEmail, which config.ts:6 defaults to owner@acme.test, the user seed.ts makes an owner. A header-less request therefore has every owner permission (finding F1).

items.prompt: Both transaction attempts reject with a Prisma P2034 error. What does the caller get?
items.answer: 409 webhook.claim_conflict, after one retry of the transaction
distractors: 500 server.internal, as the raw Prisma error reaches errorMiddleware
A third attempt, then more; it loops until the transaction commits
409 webhook.identity_conflict, the same code a payload mismatch gets
items.explanation: P2002 and P2034 count as contention (line 122). The loop runs two attempts; the second contention becomes HttpError 409 webhook.claim_conflict. Any other error is rethrown and becomes a sanitized 500.

items.prompt: You delete the "if (attempt === 1) { throw ... }" block inside the catch of processMockPaymentWebhook. What does the test suite report?
items.answer: All tests still pass, since line 130 throws the same 409 once the loop exits
distractors: The contention test fails, because the second P2034 now escapes as a raw 500
The suite hangs, as the retry loop no longer has any way to terminate
Only the replay tests fail, since attempt two now returns undefined
items.explanation: The loop is bounded by attempt < 2, so after the second contention it exits and the final throw at line 130 raises the identical webhook.claim_conflict. The branch is redundant and no test can tell the difference (chapter 04 break-it table).

items.prompt: How does the worker's attemptPayment decide whether a queued payment succeeds?
items.answer: invoice.total % 7 !== 0, with the payment created already succeeded or failed
distractors: It creates a processing payment and leaves the mock webhook to settle it later
It calls canTransitionInvoice and fails every invoice that cannot become paid
By a random draw seeded from the invoice id, retried up to five times on failure
items.explanation: jobs.ts:120 decides with invoice.total % 7 !== 0 and creates the payment with its final status. So in the running app the webhook usually meets a payment the worker already settled, which is why finding F2 is the common case.

items.prompt: POST /api/billing/invoices/:invoiceId/pay is called for a void invoice whose total is 120. What does the worker end up doing?
items.answer: It creates a succeeded payment and marks the void invoice paid
distractors: It refuses with invoice.transition_invalid, as the webhook does
Nothing, because the pay route only queues open invoices for it
It throws P2025, since findFirstOrThrow skips void invoices
items.explanation: The route queues any tenant invoice it finds, and attemptPayment only checks status === "paid" (jobs.ts:116). 120 % 7 is 1, so the payment succeeds and the invoice is set to paid: the worker bypasses the state machine the webhook enforces (finding F6).

items.prompt: Two concurrent requests carry the same idempotency-key and the same payload. What can runIdempotent do?
items.answer: Both miss the key, both run the work, then the later upsert overwrites the stored response
distractors: The second blocks on the key row's lock; it resumes only after the first request has committed
The second gets 409 idempotency.payload_conflict for reusing an existing key
Only one runs, because findUnique and the upsert share a single transaction
items.explanation: runIdempotent reads the key (line 16), runs the work (line 35), then upserts (lines 36-52), with no transaction or pending row in between: check-then-act. Two requests can both run, and update: { response } lets the second overwrite the first (finding F4).

items.prompt: Two worker processes run processOutboxBatch at the same moment. What can happen to a pending outbox event?
items.answer: Both may select the same row, so the event gets delivered twice by the pair
distractors: The second claim update fails, as it re-checks that the status is still pending
Prisma locks the selected rows, so the second worker waits until the first is done
Each worker takes a disjoint batch of 10 rows because results are ordered by date
items.explanation: findMany selects pending rows, then each is updated to processing by id alone (outbox-processor.ts:14-20). Nothing stops a second process from selecting the same rows first, so delivery is at-least-once and consumers must be idempotent (finding F8).

items.front: Every step before the first write in processMockPaymentWebhook, in order, with its refusal
items.back: Permission (403) -> parse (400) -> open the transaction -> event identity (409, or the duplicate return) -> scoped payment (404) -> scoped invoice (404) -> transition guard (409) -> first write: tx.webhookEvent.create. A refused request therefore leaves no event row.

items.front: Which invoice states may a webhook success pay, and what about an already-paid invoice?
items.back: Only open and uncollectible may transition to paid; draft and void get 409 invoice.transition_invalid. A paid invoice is not a legal source either, but invoice.status !== "paid" short-circuits the guard, so the success is processed with no invoice update.

items.front: What the mocked service suite can and cannot prove about the transaction
items.back: It proves control flow: call order, the exact where predicates, side-effect counts, the Serializable option being requested and the typed 409 after two contentions. It cannot prove PostgreSQL locking, rollback, commit ordering or a real two-request race; only the skipped integration test (TEST_DATABASE_URL) touches that.

items.front: How should a test prove the payment read is tenant scoped?
items.back: Make payment.findFirst return null (a scoped database hides the org-b row) AND assert the where object is { id, organizationId }. Returning a foreign row and expecting a rejection can hide a missing predicate. Expect 404 payment.not_found and no event, update, audit or outbox write.
